prompt: A manufacturer's new plant runs at 55% of capacity a year after opening, with no unusual downtime. The demand forecast had assumed 85%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Orders probably exceed forecast, but the plant can't keep up.
options.feedback: A plant at 55% with no unusual downtime has spare capacity, so it isn't failing to keep up.

options.text: Machine breakdowns are likely limiting output.
The forecasting team got it wrong, and that is the whole story.
options.feedback: This states one cause as certain and blames a team before any data.

options.text: Demand likely fell short of the forecast.
options.feedback: Right. With no unusual downtime, low utilization points to demand. I'd compare forecast and actual orders by customer.

explanation: The data shows the plant at 55% of capacity, against an 85% forecast, with no unusual downtime. Likely cause: demand fell short of the forecast. To test it, compare forecast and actual orders by customer. If orders match the forecast, look at production planning.
